# Tagcast 1.6.5

## Clearer track comparisons before trashing

- Track release years now appear beside upload dates in the album trash selection and its final review. Unknown years remain explicitly unknown; the album year is never substituted.
- A **Less common year** label marks known track years that differ from a strict majority on the same original disc. The comparison stays separate for each original disc, including combined album views.
- **Select different years** lets you explicitly select those tracks, then adjust and review the selection. A different year does not establish that a recording is a duplicate or unwanted: live recordings, bonus tracks and reissues may legitimately differ. Opening the view never selects or removes anything.
- The existing duplicate-copy comparison, playback, queue and save safeguards are unchanged. All new controls are translated into English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Japanese.

Album splitting introduced in 1.6.0 remains available through an album's More menu. Select tracks, review the destination and confirm; Tagcast checks both albums afterwards. Track IDs, metadata, artwork and playlist references are preserved. Splits are not transactional and have no automatic retry or Undo.

The [video walkthrough](https://tagcast.app/#walkthrough) now gives a short tour of Tagcast's main features.

## Downloads and compatibility

Standalone downloads are included for macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, Windows
x64 and Linux x64, each with a SHA-256 companion. Linux now also has a
**Debian/Ubuntu `.deb` installer**, with a desktop-menu entry and `tagcast-cli`.
Its installation, sandboxed startup and removal are checked on Ubuntu 22.04 and
24.04 before publication; the portable TAR.GZ remains available. The macOS downloads are
**Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple**; signatures, stapled tickets,
Gatekeeper and extracted application startup are checked before publication.
Windows Authenticode signing through SignPath is not active yet.

Quit the older app before upgrading. Settings and sign-in data are preserved.
Linux still requires a graphical desktop and compatible libraries. The portable
archive may require distribution-specific sandbox setup; keep Chromium's sandbox enabled. Python/browser use and the bundled `tagcast-cli` remain available.

Experimental Gapless Playback remains optional and disabled by default.
Unsupported transitions use normal playback; universal sample accuracy across
formats and platforms is not claimed. This release does not change the audio engine.

The illustrated [PDF manual](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/PDF-manual)
remains the labelled 1.4.0 edition; the Wiki documents newer features.

**Code signing policy:** macOS is Developer ID signed and notarized. SignPath
Foundation support for Windows remains pending; these Windows downloads are
unsigned. [Signing details](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast#code-signing-policy)
and [privacy policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.6.5/PRIVACY.md).
